text.p: Sundstrand Corp said Friday it expects its 1997 sales to show an increase of ten to 15 percent which will result in year earnings in a range of $2.65 to $2.85 a share.

"We continue to expect that our 1997 sales will increase between 10 percent and 15 percent, which should generate earnings per share between $2.65 and $2.85 per share, excluding previously announced restructuring charges and any future share repurchases," said Robert Jenkins, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.

Earlier today, Sundstrand reported 1997 first quarter earnings rose to $35 million or $0.58 a share from $29 million or $0.47 before a restructuring charge of $3 million or $0.05 in the 1996 period. First quarter sales increased to $389 million from $368 million in the 1996 first quarter.

Sundstrand repurchased 445,212 shares of common stock during the first quarter and has repurchased 66,800 shares thus far in the second quarter. The company said it intends to continue to repurchase shares.
First quarter operating cash flow after capital expenditures was $31 million, the company said.

First quarter sales for its aerospace segment were $212 million, up 20 percent from the first quarter of 1996 as a result of a 50 percent increase in commercial orginal equipment sales. Operating profit rose 41 percent to $38 million and operating profit margins increased to 17.9 percent from 15.3 percent during the first quarter of 1997 compared with the first quarter of 1996, it said.
Orders in the first quarter were $226 million, an increase of 28 percent compared with the first quarter of 1996 due to higher commercial aftermarket and military OEM orders.

Jenkins said, "Our commercial aerospace business remains strong especially on the OEM side. Our commercial aftermarket orders were greater then we expected in the first quarter and should this trend continue, our projections for Aerospace may prove to be slightly conservative."

As a result, he said the company is on track to meet its projection of overall Aerospace sales growth between 20 percent to 25 percent with an operating profit margin in the mid 17 percent to the mid 18 percent range for 1997.

First quarter 1997 sales for its industrial segment fell seven percent to $177 million due to lower orders during the fourth quarter of 1996 and customer delivery requirements. Operating profit was $27 million, a decline of only $2 million from the first quarter 1996 as a result of the reduced sales levels. Despite the decline, margins rose slightly to 15.3 percent from 15.2 percent in the first quarter of 1996. Orders in the first quarter were up three percent compared with the first quarter of 1996, it said.

Jenkins said, "Our industrial order trends have improved in the first quarter and quote activity has become stronger. As a result of this and customer delivery requirements, we are looking for sales improvements in our Industrial businesses during the second quarter."

He said the company continues to project sales growth of up to five percent in 1997, with operating profit margins in the 16 percent to 17 percent range, which should result in its industrial operating profit growing by five percent to 10 percent.
Sundstrand designs, makes and sells technology-based components and subsystems for aerospace and industrial markets.
